questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Why British schools are the best in the world
How to prepare for maths exams
The life of a school principal in Estonia
International school rankings and what makes some countries do well
questions.why: They talk about the Pisa rankings and what makes countries perform better in these tests.

questions.q: What does Beth think of the British education system?
options: It's quite good, but probably not the best in the world
It's the best in the world
It's very poor and needs to change completely, starting with exams
She doesn't have an opinion
questions.why: She says it's quite good, she'd change a couple of things, but it's 'maybe not the best in the world'.

questions.q: What do the Pisa tests try to show?
options: Which countries have the most teachers
Which countries teach maths, science and reading most effectively
Which schools have the best buildings
Which students will go to the best universities in their own country
questions.why: Beth says they try to show which countries are most effective at teaching maths, science and reading.

questions.q: According to journalist Sean Coughlan, why were the tests controversial at first?
options: The tests were much too difficult for most students in poorer countries
Only rich countries could take part
People doubted you could fairly compare very different countries
Teachers refused to use them
questions.why: People asked how you could possibly compare America to Luxembourg or parts of China.

questions.q: What pattern is often seen in the Pisa rankings?
options: Large Western European countries usually come first
Rich countries always do best
The most successful countries tend to be smaller
Results stay the same every time
questions.why: Beth says the most successful countries tend to be smaller, like Singapore, Estonia and Taiwan.

questions.q: Why does Sean mention a 'knowledge economy'?
options: To say that Pisa tests are not useful
To explain why countries might want to measure skills with these tests
To show that Estonia's economy still depends on a large farming industry
To describe what students study at university
questions.why: He says if you want an economy based on skills, 'this is how you measure it'.

questions.q: According to Sean, which countries tend to do well?
options: Those that get all pupils to a certain standard, whatever their background
Those that spend the most money on school buildings, teachers and technology
Those with the longest school days
Those that give the most homework
questions.why: He says countries that get all pupils to a certain standard, 'regardless of their background', do well.

questions.q: According to principal Rando Kuustik, what is one reason for Estonia's success?
options: Students start school very early
Schools use lots of technology
Teachers are paid very well compared with other countries
Students are not separated into groups by ability
questions.why: He says teaching by level or ability segregates people, and not doing that is why Estonia is successful.
